title: Parser tolerance — skip noise lines, don't reject whole block
trigger: A line-based parser rejects an entire record/block because one line doesn't match the expected format, losing all valid data in that block
principle: Parsers must tolerate non-standard formats — skip noise lines instead of rejecting the whole block when a single line doesn't match. Real-world data (subtitle sources, logs, CSV exports) has format variants: literal placeholders instead of numeric indices, missing fields, extra metadata lines. Rejecting the block loses the entire record; skipping the noise line preserves it. The structural anchor (regex matching timing/format) is the anchor — advance the line index until the anchor is found, and only reject the block when lines run out without an anchor.

cases.context: SRT source uses literal 'None' instead of a numeric cue index on the first line of each block; the parser treats it as the timing line, fails to parse timing, and skips every cue → 0 cues total

applyFor: Subtitle parsers (SRT, VTT, ASS — fansub sites with format variants)
Log parsers (log lines with extra metadata, missing fields)
CSV/TSV parsers (rows with extra columns, missing delimiters)
Any line-based parser with a structural anchor (regex match) — advance past noise lines, don't reject the block on the first non-match
